candidates.description: Textream is a free macOS teleprompter app for streamers, interviewers, and presenters. It highlights your script in real-time as you speak, displayed in a beautiful Dynamic Island overlay. With extensible features.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
Textream

A free teleprompter for Mac, iPhone, and iPad.

Built for streamers, interviewers, presenters, and podcasters.

Download · iPhone & iPad · Features · How It Works · Build · Privacy

--- ## What is Textream? Textream is a free, open-source teleprompter that guides you through your script with three modes: **word tracking** (highlights each word as you say it), **classic** (constant-speed auto-scroll), and **voice-activated** (scrolls while you speak, pauses when you're silent). The Mac app displays your text in a sleek **Dynamic Island-style overlay**, a **draggable floating window**, or **fullscreen on a Sidecar iPad**. The iPhone and iPad app adds near-camera reading and presenter-only camera recording. Paste your script, hit play, and start speaking. When you're done, the overlay closes automatically. ## Download **[Download Textream from the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/textream/id6800061488)** for Mac, iPhone, and iPad. Or **[download the latest .dmg from GitHub Releases](https://github.com/f/textream/releases/latest)**. Or install with Homebrew: ```bash brew install textream ``` > Requires **macOS 15 Sequoia** or later. Works on Apple Silicon and Intel. ## iOS 26 Companion The Textream companion for iPhone and iPad is part of the same universal App Store listing as the Mac app. - **Portrait and landscape** — A fullscreen teleprompter layout adapts to both orientations. - **Mirror mode for teleprompter glass** — Read mode can flip the prompt horizontally, vertically, or on both axes whenever the device is in landscape. The prompt controls stay readable, and a compact ↔ button opens live mirror, position, text-size, speed, and playback-control settings. - **Eye-contact reading position** — The active line sits just below the front camera by default, or can be centered in Prompter Settings. - **The same three guidance modes** — Word Tracking, Classic auto-scroll, and Voice-Activa

# Whisper ASR Webservice

[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ahmetoner/whisper-asr-webservice.svg)](https://github.com/ahmetoner/whisper-asr-webservice/releases)
[![Docker Pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice.svg)](https://hub.docker.com/r/onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice)
[![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/ahmetoner/whisper-asr-webservice/test.yml?label=test)](https://github.com/ahmetoner/whisper-asr-webservice/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/ahmetoner/whisper-asr-webservice.svg)](LICENCE)

A self-hosted REST API for speech recognition, translation and language identification based on
[OpenAI Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper). It runs as a Docker container on CPU or NVIDIA GPU.

## Features

- Three engines: OpenAI Whisper, Faster Whisper and WhisperX
- Transcription in every language Whisper supports, and translation into English
- Language detection with a confidence score
- Output as plain text, JSON, WebVTT, SRT or TSV
- Word-level timestamps, voice activity detection (VAD) and speaker diarization
- Accepts any audio or video file FFmpeg can decode
- Optional API key authentication
- Unloads the model when idle to free memory
- Interactive API documentation (Swagger UI)

## Quick Start

CPU (amd64 and arm64):

```shell
docker run -d -p 9000:9000 \
  -e ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper \
  -e ASR_MODEL=base \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest
```

NVIDIA GPU (amd64, requires the [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html)):

```shell
docker run -d --gpus all -p 9000:9000 \
  -e ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper \
  -e ASR_MODEL=base \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest-gpu
```

Open <http://localhost:9000/docs> to use the API from your browser, or send a request directly:

```shell
curl -F "audio_file=@audio.mp3" "http://localhost:9000/asr?output=json"
```

## Engines

| Engine                                                       | `ASR_ENGINE`               | Notes                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| [OpenAI Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper)          | `openai_whisper` (default) | Reference implementation

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar [**Live demo**](https://aura.kyutai.org/) · [**Project page**](http://kyutai.org/aura) · [**Paper**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26540) · [**AURA-1.3B**](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/AURA-1.3B) · [**AURA-5B**](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/AURA-5B) · [**AURA-1.3B teacher**](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/AURA-1.3B-Teacher-TalkVerse) · [**AURA dataset**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/kyutai/AURA-Dataset) Nathaniel Cohen1,2, Nicolas Dufour1, Amélie Royer1, Alasdair Newson2, Patrick Pérez3*
1Kyutai · 2Sorbonne Université, ISIR · 3Google DeepMind · *work done while at Kyutai
*BMVC 2026* AURA turns a single portrait image and a speech audio stream into a talking-head video, **chunk by chunk, in streaming**. Each chunk needs only its own audio, with no multi-second look-ahead. The models are 4-step **causal** students distilled from 50-step bidirectional speech-to-video teachers. A rolling KV cache keeps the first chunk as an identity anchor plus the most recent chunk, so memory stays constant on arbitrarily long streams. Samples are on the [project page](http://kyutai.org/aura), and you can talk to AURA-1.3B combined with our cascaded voice model Unmute in the [live demo](https://aura.kyutai.org/). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de813f1c-0836-4c17-9851-096e8dfcbdd9 ## Models | Model | Teacher | Audio encoder | Output | Speed (paper, 1× H100) | Weights license | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [AURA-1.3B](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/AURA-1.3B) | [AURA-1.3B-Teacher-TalkVerse](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/AURA-1.3B-Teacher-TalkVerse) (on [Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B)) | [Mimi](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/mimi) | 576p, 16 fps | **20.7 fps (real time)**, 23× faster than its teacher | CC BY-NC 4.0 | | [AURA-5B](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/AURA-5B) | [TalkVerse-S2V-5B](https://huggingface.co/snap-research/talkverse-s2v-5b) (on [Wan2.2-TI2V-5B](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B)) | [wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-english](https://huggingface.co/jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-english) | 720p, 25 fps | 9.7 fps, 17× faster than its teacher | Snap Inc. candidates.readme_excerpt:
# ✈️ AI Travel Itinerary Generator

An intelligent travel planning application that generates personalized tourist itineraries based on the user's destination, budget, available time, and trip duration.

## 🌍 Project Overview

AI Travel Itinerary Generator helps users plan their trips by recommending suitable tourist destinations and organizing them into a day-wise travel itinerary.

The application considers user preferences and travel constraints to make trip planning easier and more convenient.

## ✨ Features

- **Destination-Based Recommendations:** Enter a destination state to discover tourist attractions.
- **Budget-Based Planning:** Generate recommendations according to the available budget.
- **Time-Based Selection:** Consider available visiting hours per day.
- **Day-Wise Itinerary:** Organize selected tourist places across multiple days.
- **Tourist Place Information:** View city, category, Google rating, entrance fee, visit duration, best time to visit, and significance.
- **Interactive Web Interface:** User-friendly black and blue themed frontend.

## 🛠️ Technologies Used

- Python
- Flask
- Pandas
- HTML
- CSS
- Machine Learning / Data Preprocessing

## 📂 Project Structure

```text
AI_Travel_Itinerary/
│
├── app.py
├── eda.py
├── preprocess.py
├── preprocess_ml.py
├── feature_scaling.py
├── feature_selection.py
├── recommendation.py
├── itinerary_generator.py
│
├── dataset/
│   ├── Top Indian Places to Visit.csv
│   └── cleaned_travel_data.csv
│
├── templates/
│   ├── index.html
│   └── result.html
│
├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## ⚙️ Installation and Setup

### 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SebaVarshini/AI_Travel_Itinerary.git
```

### 2. Navigate to the Project Folder

```bash
cd AI_Travel_Itinerary
```

### 3. Create a Virtual Environment

```bash
python -m venv venv
```

### 4. Activate the Virtual Environment

Windows:

```bash
venv\Scripts\activate
```

### 5. Install Dependencies

```bash
pip install flask pandas numpy scikit-learn
```

### 6. Run the Application

```bash
python app.py
```

Open your browser and visit:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:5000/
```

## 🚀 How It Works

1. Enter the destination state.
2. Provide the total travel budget.
3. Enter available visiting hours per day.
4. Select the number of travel days.
5. Generate the personalized itinerary.
6. Explore recommended tourist destinations and day-wise travel details.

## 🎯 Project Objective

To simplify travel planning by combining data

**A coding agent skill.** Drop source documents into `raw/` and tell the agent to ingest them — it reads them, extracts knowledge, and builds a persistent interlinked wiki. Every new source makes the wiki richer. You never write it.

> Most knowledge tools make you search your own notes. This one reads everything you've collected and writes a structured wiki that compounds over time — cross-references already built, contradictions already flagged, synthesis already done.

```
ingest raw/papers/attention-is-all-you-need.md
```

```
wiki/
├── index.md          catalog of all pages — updated on every ingest
├── log.md            append-only record of every operation
├── overview.md       living synthesis across all sources
├── sources/          one summary page per source document
├── entities/         people, companies, projects — auto-created
├── concepts/         ideas, frameworks, methods — auto-created
└── syntheses/        query answers filed back as wiki pages
graph/
├── graph.json        persistent node/edge data (SHA256-cached)
└── graph.html        interactive vis.js visualization — open in any browser
```

- [awesome-jev-by-typesafe](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/awesome-jev-by-typesafe) — typed semantic retrieval, citation checks, and confidence-aware routing for agent knowledge workflows

## Install

**Requires:** [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code), [Codex](https://openai.com/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli), or any agent that reads a config file.

# Codex plugin for Claude Code

Use Codex from inside Claude Code for code reviews or to delegate tasks to Codex.

This plugin is for Claude Code users who want an easy way to start using Codex from the workflow
they already have.

<video src="./docs/plugin-demo.webm" controls muted playsinline autoplay></video>

## What You Get

- `/codex:review` for a normal read-only Codex review
- `/codex:adversarial-review` for a steerable challenge review
- `/codex:rescue`, `/codex:transfer`, `/codex:status`, `/codex:result`, and `/codex:cancel` to delegate work, hand off sessions, and manage background jobs

## Requirements

- **ChatGPT subscription (incl. Free) or OpenAI API key.**
  - Usage will contribute to your Codex usage limits. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/codex/pricing).
- **Node.js 18.18 or later**

## Install

Add the marketplace in Claude Code:

```bash
/plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc
```

Install the plugin:

```bash
/plugin install codex@openai-codex
```

Reload plugins:

```bash
/reload-plugins
```

Then run:

```bash
/codex:setup
```

`/codex:setup` will tell you whether Codex is ready. If Codex is missing and npm is available, it can offer to install Codex for you.

If you prefer to install Codex yourself, use:

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex
```

If Codex is installed but not logged in yet, run:

```bash
!codex login
```

After install, you should see:

- the slash commands listed below
- the `codex:codex-rescue` subagent in `/agents`

One simple first run is:

```bash
/codex:review --background
/codex:status
/codex:result
```

## Usage

### `/codex:review`

Runs a normal Codex review on your current work. It gives you the same quality of code review as running `/review` inside Codex directly.

> [!NOTE]
> Code review especially for multi-file changes might take a while. It's generally recommended to run it in the background.

Use it when you want:

- a review of your current uncommitted changes
- a review of your branch compared to a base branch like `main`

Use `--base <ref>` for branch review. It also supports `--wait` and `--background`. It is not steerable and does not take custom focus text. Use [`/codex:adversarial-review`](#codexadversarial-review) when you want to challenge a specific decision or risk area.

Examples:

```bash
/codex:review
/codex:review --base main
/codex:review --background
```

candidates.description: A lightweight, powerful framework for multi-agent workflows and voice agents
candidates.readme_excerpt: # OpenAI Agents SDK (JavaScript/TypeScript) [![npm version](https://badge.fury.io/js/@openai%2Fagents.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/js/@openai%2Fagents) [![CI](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/actions/workflows/test.yml) The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight yet powerful framework for building multi-agent workflows in JavaScript/TypeScript. It is provider-agnostic, supporting OpenAI APIs and more. ## Core concepts 1. [**Agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/agents): LLMs configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, and handoffs 1. [**Sandbox Agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/sandbox-agents): Agents paired with a filesystem workspace and sandbox environment for longer-running work 1. [**Realtime Agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/voice-agents/quickstart/): Low-latency agents for spoken interactions, with tools, guardrails, handoffs, and conversation history 1. **[Agents as tools](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tools/#4-agents-as-tools) / [Handoffs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/handoffs/)**: Delegating to other agents for specific tasks 1. [**Tools**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tools/): Various Tools let agents take actions (functions, MCP, hosted tools) 1. [**Guardrails**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/guardrails/): Configurable safety checks for input and output validation 1. # User Interview Guide skill for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor

A free agent skill that turns what you need to learn into a neutral 1:1 user interview guide: core questions, optional probes, a moderator card and a debrief. It works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any agent that supports skills.

## Install

```bash
npx skills add uxpilot-ai/user-interview-skill
```

Or copy the `skills/user-interview-guide` folder into your agent's skills folder (for Claude Code, `~/.claude/skills/`).

## What it does

- Asks what you need to learn and how you will use the answers, one question at a time.
- Picks the right kind of interview: problem discovery, retained value, adoption and churn, switching, or concept reaction.
- Writes neutral questions anchored in real past events, and flags leading, hypothetical, double-barrelled or overloaded ones.
- Delivers a timeboxed guide, a compact moderator card and a five-minute debrief.
- Tells you when an interview is the wrong method, for example to measure how common something is or to test what caused a change.

## Example prompts

- "Write a 30-minute interview guide to learn why trial users don't activate."
- "Review these interview questions for leading or hypothetical wording."
- "I'm talking to three churned customers tomorrow. Make me a guide."
- "Help me plan switching interviews with people who moved to a competitor."

## What's inside

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | The flow: clarify the goal, choose a path, draft the guide |
| `references/interview-modes.md` | How the guide changes for discovery, retention, churn, switching and concept interviews |
| `references/question-design.md` | Building a guide in seven passes, and 15 kinds of weak question with rewrites |
| `references/moderation.md` | Running the session, common moderator mistakes, remote calls |
| `references/recruiting-and-consent.md` | Participant criteria, screeners, consent and recording |
| `references/evidence-signals.md` | What interviews can and cannot prove, and how to debrief |
| `assets/interview-guide-template.md` | A template for a full research round |

## Made by UX Pilot

[UX Pilot](https://uxpilot.ai/?utm_source=user-interview-guide&utm_medium=readme) is an AI UI design tool. When your interviews point to a product change, it can turn your notes into screens, user flows and clickable prototypes, and predict where people will look with an attention heatmap.

# Eliza on Vibestack

This workspace specifies Eliza v4 on Vibestack: the kernel, the agent host,
the device image, the cloud services and the assistant plugins. Agents run
on the device; the cloud serves identity, billing and model access. The
specification covers requirements, Quint models, and the generated
contracts for the VibeLang and Effect implementation.

Start with [the package specifications](spec/index.md),
[the agent procedure](AGENTS.md) and [the spec reference](SPEC.md).
The source baseline is Eliza commit
`72fed7e4069ecd35d61d886ab6eec5c02c137517`. The orphan `vibestack` branch
starts from elizaOS/eliza-vibestack commit
`71d7b30f404b91d7ec48741ac288d6c8d911f3e2`; its toolchain is merged from
lalalune/vibestack commit `45cc5c35d58b8dc18b0a57b116fde2386eef5528`.

The vendored Vibestack toolchain is synchronized with upstream commit
`09f0b412ed892c981b546d646826260d9012ef62`. Eliza retains its [repository lint and verification policies](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Setup and verification

Use Node 26, pnpm 10.24.0 and Dafny 4.11.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm gen
pnpm check
pnpm verify
```

`pnpm check` generates the contracts, checks model traces and replay,
proves safety obligations, runs available journeys, and lists changes for
review. `pnpm accept` records the user's review. Each package's shell is
implemented from its accepted specification.

### Android password recovery fixture

The Passwords instrumentation uses Android Keystore and a disposable PGlite
Cloud Worker. Use an unlocked Android 15 or later test emulator with a screen
lock and install the test APK from the portable module:

```sh
ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554 gradle -p packages/os/android/passwords/test/fixture \
  -PcapacitorAndroidDir=/path/to/installed/@capacitor/android \
  :elizaos-capacitor-passwords:installDebugAndroidTest
```

Run the focused journey from the Eliza root after `pnpm gen --owner cloud`:

```sh
PASSWORD_ANDROID_FIXTURE=emulator-5554 pnpm --filter @elizaos/cloud exec \
  vitest run test/password-backup.test.vibe -t 'Android cold start'
```

For a restore into a second Android Keystore, prepare two independently created
emulators using the steps above. Set `PASSWORD_ANDROID_FIXTURE=emulator-5554,emulator-5556`
in the same command. The first device saves the vault and the second enrolls a
fresh device grant and restores into its empty vault. A single serial exercises
both phases in separate processes on that emulator.
